sanskrit: gaccha gaccheti tāṃ śālvaḥ punaḥ punar abhāṣata bibhemi bhīṣmāt suśroṇi tvaṃ ca bhīṣmaparigrahaḥ
english: "Go, go!" Śālva said to her again and again. "I fear Bhīṣma, fair-hipped one, and you are Bhīṣma's prize."

sanskrit: evam uktā tu sā tena śālvenādīrghadarśinā niścakrāma purād dīnā rudatī kurarī yathā
english: Thus addressed by Śālva, that man of short sight, she went forth from the city, wretched, weeping like an osprey.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca sā niṣkramantī nagarāc cintayām āsa bhārata pṛthivyāṃ nāsti yuvatir viṣamasthatarā mayā bāndhavair viprahīnāsmi śālvena ca nirākṛtā
english: Bhīṣma said: As she went out from the city, O Bhārata, she thought: "On this earth there is no maiden more wretchedly placed than I. Bereft of my kinsmen, I am spurned by Śālva as well."

sanskrit: na ca śakyaṃ punar gantuṃ mayā vāraṇasāhvayam anujñātāsmi bhīṣmeṇa śālvam uddiśya kāraṇam
english: "Nor can I go back to the city named for the elephant, for I was released by Bhīṣma on Śālva's account."

sanskrit: kiṃ nu garhāmy athātmānam atha bhīṣmaṃ durāsadam āho svit pitaraṃ mūḍhaṃ yo me 'kārṣīt svayaṃvaram
english: "Whom then shall I blame—myself, or the unassailable Bhīṣma, or my foolish father, who arranged for me a self-choice of husband?"

sanskrit: mamāyaṃ svakṛto doṣo yāhaṃ bhīṣmarathāt tadā pravṛtte vaiśase yuddhe śālvārthaṃ nāpataṃ purā tasyeyaṃ phalanirvṛttir yad āpannāsmi mūḍhavat
english: "This is a fault of my own making, that long ago, when the deadly battle was joined, I did not leap from Bhīṣma's chariot for Śālva's sake. This is the fruit ripened of that, that I have come to ruin like a fool."

sanskrit: dhig bhīṣmaṃ dhik ca me mandaṃ pitaraṃ mūḍhacetasam yenāhaṃ vīryaśulkena paṇyastrīvat praveritā
english: "A curse on Bhīṣma, and a curse on my dull-witted, foolish father, by whom I was flung forth like a woman for sale, with valor as the bride-price."

sanskrit: dhiṅ māṃ dhik śālvarājānaṃ dhig dhātāram athāpi ca yeṣāṃ durnītabhāvena prāptāsmy āpadam uttamām
english: "A curse on me, a curse on King Śālva, and a curse on the Creator too, by whose ill-conduct I have come to this utmost calamity."

sanskrit: sarvathā bhāgadheyāni svāni prāpnoti mānavaḥ anayasyāsya tu mukhaṃ bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo mama
english: "In every way a mortal reaps his own allotted portions; yet the fountainhead of this misfortune of mine is Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu."

sanskrit: sā bhīṣme pratikartavyam ahaṃ paśyāmi sāṃpratam tapasā vā yudhā vāpi duḥkhahetuḥ sa me mataḥ ko nu bhīṣmaṃ yudhā jetum utsaheta mahīpatiḥ
english: "I now see that vengeance must be wrought upon Bhīṣma, whether by austerity or by war—for I deem him the cause of my sorrow. Yet what king would dare to conquer Bhīṣma in battle?"

sanskrit: evaṃ sā pariniścitya jagāma nagarād bahiḥ āśramaṃ puṇyaśīlānāṃ tāpasānāṃ mahātmanām tatas tām avasad rātriṃ tāpasaiḥ parivāritā
english: Having thus resolved, she went forth from the city to the hermitage of holy-natured, great-souled ascetics; and there she passed the night, surrounded by the ascetics.

sanskrit: ācakhyau ca yathā vṛttaṃ sarvam ātmani bhārata vistareṇa mahābāho nikhilena śucismitā haraṇaṃ ca visargaṃ ca śālvena ca visarjanam
english: And she told them all that had befallen her, O mighty-armed Bhārata, fully and in detail—she of the bright smile told of her seizure, her release, and her dismissal by Śālva.

sanskrit: tatas tatra mahān āsīd brāhmaṇaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ śaikhāvatyas tapovṛddhaḥ śāstre cāraṇyake guruḥ
english: Now there was there a great Brāhmaṇa of firm vows, Śaikhāvatya, grown old in austerity, a master of the forest-lore.

sanskrit: ārtāṃ tām āha sa muniḥ śaikhāvatyo mahātapāḥ niḥśvasantīṃ satīṃ bālāṃ duḥkhaśokaparāyaṇām
english: To her in her distress that sage Śaikhāvatya, of great austerity, spoke—to the virtuous, sighing girl wholly given over to grief and sorrow:

sanskrit: evaṃ gate kiṃ nu bhadre śakyaṃ kartuṃ tapasvibhiḥ āśramasthair mahābhāgais taponityair mahātmabhiḥ
english: "Things being so, good lady, what can be done by ascetics—by the blessed great-souled ones who dwell in the hermitage and are ever devoted to austerity?"

sanskrit: sā tv enam abravīd rājan kriyatāṃ madanugrahaḥ pravrājitum ihecchāmi tapas tapsyāmi duścaram
english: And she said to him, O king: "Let a favor be granted me. I wish to go forth as a recluse here; I shall practice austerity hard to perform."

sanskrit: mayaivaitāni karmāṇi pūrvadeheṣu mūḍhayā kṛtāni nūnaṃ pāpāni teṣām etat phalaṃ dhruvam
english: "Surely these evil deeds were done by me, deluded, in former bodies; this is the certain fruit of them."

sanskrit: notsaheyaṃ punar gantuṃ svajanaṃ prati tāpasāḥ pratyākhyātā nirānandā śālvena ca nirākṛtā
english: "I cannot bear to go back to my own people, O ascetics—rejected, joyless, and spurned by Śālva."

sanskrit: upadiṣṭam ihecchāmi tāpasyaṃ vītakalmaṣāḥ yuṣmābhir devasaṃkāśāḥ kṛpā bhavatu vo mayi
english: "I wish to be taught the ascetic life here by you, O sinless ones who are like gods. Let your compassion rest upon me."

sanskrit: sa tām āśvāsayat kanyāṃ dṛṣṭāntāgamahetubhiḥ sāntvayām āsa kāryaṃ ca pratijajñe dvijaiḥ saha
english: He comforted the maiden with examples and with reasons drawn from scripture, soothed her, and together with the other Brāhmaṇas pledged to undertake her cause.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tatas te tāpasāḥ sarve kāryavanto 'bhavaṃs tadā tāṃ kanyāṃ cintayanto vai kiṃ kāryam iti dharmiṇaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Then all those ascetics, righteous men, became intent upon the matter, pondering concerning that maiden, "What is to be done?"

sanskrit: ke cid āhuḥ pitur veśma nīyatām iti tāpasāḥ ke cid asmadupālambhe matiṃ cakrur dvijottamāḥ
english: Some of the ascetics said, "Let her be taken to her father's house"; some of the foremost of the twice-born set their minds on rebuking us.

sanskrit: ke cic chālvapatiṃ gatvā niyojyam iti menire neti ke cid vyavasyanti pratyākhyātā hi tena sā
english: Some thought that they should go to the lord of Śālva and constrain him; others resolved against it, since she had been rejected by him.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate kiṃ nu śakyaṃ bhadre kartuṃ manīṣibhiḥ punar ūcuś ca te sarve tāpasāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ
english: "Things being so, good lady, what can be done by us, the wise?" And then all those ascetics of firm vows spoke again:

sanskrit: alaṃ pravrajiteneha bhadre śṛṇu hitaṃ vacaḥ ito gacchasva bhadraṃ te pitur eva niveśanam
english: "Enough of renunciation here, good lady; hear our wholesome counsel. Go from here—blessings on you—to your own father's dwelling."

sanskrit: pratipatsyati rājā sa pitā te yad anantaram tatra vatsyasi kalyāṇi sukhaṃ sarvaguṇānvitā na ca te 'nyā gatir nyāyyā bhaved bhadre yathā pitā
english: "Your father the king will see to whatever comes next. There you shall dwell in happiness, fair one, possessed of every comfort. No other refuge would be fitting for you, good lady, as your father is."

sanskrit: patir vāpi gatir nāryāḥ pitā vā varavarṇini gatiḥ patiḥ samasthāyā viṣame tu pitā gatiḥ
english: "A husband or a father is a woman's refuge, fair-complexioned one: when her fortunes are even, the husband is her refuge; but in adversity, the father is her refuge."

sanskrit: pravrajyā hi suduḥkheyaṃ sukumāryā viśeṣataḥ rājaputryāḥ prakṛtyā ca kumāryās tava bhāmini
english: "The renunciant life is full of hardship, especially for a delicate woman—and by nature for a king's daughter, and for a maiden such as you, O proud lady."

sanskrit: bhadre doṣā hi vidyante bahavo varavarṇini āśrame vai vasantyās te na bhaveyuḥ pitur gṛhe
english: "Good lady, fair one, many dangers exist for one dwelling in a hermitage; these would not be so in your father's house."

sanskrit: tatas tu te 'bruvan vākyaṃ brāhmaṇās tāṃ tapasvinīm tvām ihaikākinīṃ dṛṣṭvā nirjane gahane vane prārthayiṣyanti rājendrās tasmān maivaṃ manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Then the Brāhmaṇas spoke this word to her, the ascetic woman: "Seeing you here alone in this deserted, dense forest, great kings will woo you; therefore do not set your mind on this."

sanskrit: ambovāca na śakyaṃ kāśinagarīṃ punar gantuṃ pitur gṛhān avajñātā bhaviṣyāmi bāndhavānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: Ambā said: "I cannot return to the city of Kāśi, to my father's house. I would become an object of contempt to my kinsmen—there is no doubt of it."

sanskrit: uṣitā hy anyathā bālye pitur veśmani tāpasāḥ nāhaṃ gamiṣye bhadraṃ vas tatra yatra pitā mama tapas taptum abhīpsāmi tāpasaiḥ paripālitā
english: "In a different way I dwelt in my childhood in my father's house, O ascetics. I shall not go—blessings on you—to where my father is. I wish to perform austerity, guarded by ascetics."

sanskrit: yathā pare 'pi me loke na syād evaṃ mahātyayaḥ daurbhāgyaṃ brāhmaṇaśreṣṭhās tasmāt tapsyāmy ahaṃ tapaḥ
english: "So that in the next world too there may not be for me this same great ruin and misfortune, O best of Brāhmaṇas—therefore shall I practice austerity."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity evaṃ teṣu vipreṣu cintayatsu tathā tathā rājarṣis tad vanaṃ prāptas tapasvī hotravāhanaḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: While those Brāhmaṇas were thus pondering this way and that, the royal sage Hotravāhana, an ascetic, came to that forest.

sanskrit: tatas te tāpasāḥ sarve pūjayanti sma taṃ nṛpam pūjābhiḥ svāgatādyābhir āsanenodakena ca
english: Then all those ascetics honored that king with the rites of hospitality—with welcome and the rest, with a seat and with water.

sanskrit: tasyopaviṣṭasya tato viśrāntasyopaśṛṇvataḥ punar eva kathāṃ cakruḥ kanyāṃ prati vanaukasaḥ
english: When he was seated and rested and listening, the forest-dwellers once again took up their talk concerning the maiden.

sanskrit: ambāyās tāṃ kathāṃ śrutvā kāśirājñaś ca bhārata sa vepamāna utthāya mātur asyāḥ pitā tadā tāṃ kanyām aṅkam āropya paryāśvāsayata prabho
english: Hearing that story of Ambā and of the king of Kāśi, O Bhārata, he—the father of her mother—rose up trembling, and taking the maiden upon his lap, he comforted her, O lord.

sanskrit: sa tām apṛcchat kārtsnyena vyasanotpattim āditaḥ sā ca tasmai yathāvṛttaṃ vistareṇa nyavedayat
english: He asked her in full about the origin of her misfortune from the beginning, and she related to him in detail all that had happened.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa rājarṣir abhūd duḥkhaśokasamanvitaḥ kāryaṃ ca pratipede tan manasā sumahātapāḥ
english: Then that royal sage was filled with grief and sorrow, and that one of great austerity resolved in his mind upon the deed to be done.

sanskrit: abravīd vepamānaś ca kanyām ārtāṃ suduḥkhitaḥ mā gāḥ pitṛgṛhaṃ bhadre mātus te janako hy aham
english: And trembling, in deep sorrow, he said to the afflicted maiden: "Do not go to your father's house, good lady; for I am your mother's father."

sanskrit: duḥkhaṃ chetsyāmi te 'haṃ vai mayi vartasva putrike paryāptaṃ te manaḥ putri yad evaṃ pariśuṣyasi
english: "I shall cut away your sorrow; depend upon me, little daughter. Enough has your mind, my child, been thus withered with grief."

sanskrit: gaccha madvacanād rāmaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ tapasvinam rāmas tava mahad duḥkhaṃ śokaṃ cāpanayiṣyati haniṣyati raṇe bhīṣmaṃ na kariṣyati ced vacaḥ
english: "Go at my word to Rāma, son of Jamadagni, the ascetic. Rāma will take away your great grief and sorrow; he will slay Bhīṣma in battle if he will not heed his word."

sanskrit: taṃ gaccha bhārgavaśreṣṭhaṃ kālāgnisamatejasam pratiṣṭhāpayitā sa tvāṃ same pathi mahātapāḥ
english: "Go to that best of the Bhārgavas, whose splendor equals the fire of doom. That one of great austerity will set you again upon an even path."

sanskrit: tatas tu sasvaraṃ bāṣpam utsṛjantī punaḥ punaḥ abravīt pitaraṃ mātuḥ sā tadā hotravāhanam
english: Then, shedding tears aloud again and again, she spoke to her mother's father, Hotravāhana:

sanskrit: abhivādayitvā śirasā gamiṣye tava śāsanāt api nāmādya paśyeyam āryaṃ taṃ lokaviśrutam
english: "Having bowed my head, I shall go at your command. But can I now even behold that noble one, renowned throughout the world?"

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca tīvraṃ duḥkhaṃ me haniṣyati sa bhārgavaḥ etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotum atha yāsyāmi tatra vai
english: "And how shall that Bhārgava destroy my keen sorrow? This I wish to hear, and then indeed I shall go there."

sanskrit: hotravāhana uvāca rāmaṃ drakṣyasi vatse tvaṃ jāmadagnyaṃ mahāvane ugre tapasi vartantaṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ mahābalam
english: Hotravāhana said: "You shall see Rāma, son of Jamadagni, my child, in the great forest, engaged in fierce austerity—true to his word, of mighty strength."

sanskrit: mahendre vai giriśreṣṭhe rāmaṃ nityam upāsate ṛṣayo vedaviduṣo gandharvāpsarasas tathā
english: "On Mahendra, the best of mountains, sages versed in the Vedas ever attend upon Rāma, and Gandharvas and Apsarases too."

sanskrit: tatra gacchasva bhadraṃ te brūyāś cainaṃ vaco mama abhivādya pūrvaṃ śirasā tapovṛddhaṃ dṛḍhavratam
english: "Go there—blessings on you—and speak to him this word of mine, having first bowed your head to him, grown old in austerity, of firm vows."

sanskrit: brūyāś cainaṃ punar bhadre yat te kāryaṃ manīṣitam mayi saṃkīrtite rāmaḥ sarvaṃ tat te kariṣyati
english: "And tell him further, good lady, whatever purpose you have in mind; when I am named, Rāma will do all of it for you."

sanskrit: mama rāmaḥ sakhā vatse prītiyuktaḥ suhṛc ca me jamadagnisuto vīraḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ
english: "Rāma is my friend, my child, bound to me in affection, and my well-wisher—the heroic son of Jamadagni, the foremost of all who bear weapons."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kanyāṃ tu pārthive hotravāhane akṛtavraṇaḥ prādurāsīd rāmasyānucaraḥ priyaḥ
english: While the king Hotravāhana was thus speaking to the maiden, Akṛtavraṇa appeared, the dear companion of Rāma.

sanskrit: tatas te munayaḥ sarve samuttasthuḥ sahasraśaḥ sa ca rājā vayovṛddhaḥ sṛñjayo hotravāhanaḥ
english: Then all those sages rose up by the thousands, and that aged king Hotravāhana, of the Sṛñjayas, as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ pṛṣṭvā yathānyāyam anyonyaṃ te vanaukasaḥ sahitā bharataśreṣṭha niṣeduḥ parivārya tam
english: Then, having greeted one another in due form, those forest-dwellers, O best of the Bhāratas, sat down together, surrounding him.

sanskrit: tatas te kathayām āsuḥ kathās tās tā manoramāḥ kāntā divyāś ca rājendra prītiharṣamudā yutāḥ
english: Then they told one tale after another, delightful, lovely and sublime, O great king, full of love and joy and gladness.

sanskrit: tataḥ kathānte rājarṣir mahātmā hotravāhanaḥ rāmaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ maharṣīṇām apṛcchad akṛtavraṇam
english: Then, at the end of the talk, the great-souled royal sage Hotravāhana asked Akṛtavraṇa about Rāma, foremost of the great sages:

sanskrit: kva saṃprati mahābāho jāmadagnyaḥ pratāpavān akṛtavraṇa śakyo vai draṣṭuṃ vedavidāṃ varaḥ
english: "Where now, O mighty-armed Akṛtavraṇa, is the valiant son of Jamadagni? Can he be seen—he, the best of those who know the Vedas?"

sanskrit: akṛtavraṇa uvāca bhavantam eva satataṃ rāmaḥ kīrtayati prabho sṛñjayo me priyasakho rājarṣir iti pārthiva
english: Akṛtavraṇa said: "Rāma is ever speaking of you yourself, my lord—'the Sṛñjaya is my dear friend, a royal sage,' so he says, O king."

sanskrit: iha rāmaḥ prabhāte śvo bhaviteti matir mama draṣṭāsy enam ihāyāntaṃ tava darśanakāṅkṣayā
english: "It is my thought that Rāma will be here tomorrow at dawn; you shall see him coming here, eager for the sight of you."

sanskrit: iyaṃ ca kanyā rājarṣe kimarthaṃ vanam āgatā kasya ceyaṃ tava ca kā bhavatīcchāmi veditum
english: "And this maiden, O royal sage—for what purpose has she come to the forest? Whose is she, and what is she to you? I wish to know."

sanskrit: hotravāhana uvāca dauhitrīyaṃ mama vibho kāśirājasutā śubhā jyeṣṭhā svayaṃvare tasthau bhaginībhyāṃ sahānagha
english: Hotravāhana said: "This is my daughter's daughter, my lord—the fair daughter of the king of Kāśi. The eldest, she stood at the self-choice along with her sisters, O sinless one."

sanskrit: iyam ambeti vikhyātā jyeṣṭhā kāśipateḥ sutā ambikāmbālike tv anye yavīyasyau tapodhana
english: "This eldest daughter of the lord of Kāśi is known as Ambā; the other two, the younger, are Ambikā and Ambālikā, O you whose wealth is austerity."

sanskrit: sametaṃ pārthivaṃ kṣatraṃ kāśipuryāṃ tato 'bhavat kanyānimittaṃ brahmarṣe tatrāsīd utsavo mahān
english: "The kingly warrior-host of the kings had gathered then in the city of Kāśi; on account of the maidens, O Brahmā-sage, there was a great festival there."

sanskrit: tataḥ kila mahāvīryo bhīṣmaḥ śāṃtanavo nṛpān avākṣipya mahātejās tisraḥ kanyā jahāra tāḥ
english: "Then, it is said, the mighty Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, of great splendor, scattered the kings and carried off those three maidens."

sanskrit: nirjitya pṛthivīpālān atha bhīṣmo gajāhvayam ājagāma viśuddhātmā kanyābhiḥ saha bhārata
english: "Having conquered the rulers of the earth, Bhīṣma of pure soul came then to the city named for the elephant together with the maidens, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: satyavatyai nivedyātha vivāhārtham anantaram bhrātur vicitravīryasya samājñāpayata prabhuḥ
english: "Having then made them known to Satyavatī, the lord forthwith commanded that they be married to his brother Vicitravīrya."

sanskrit: tato vaivāhikaṃ dṛṣṭvā kanyeyaṃ samupārjitam abravīt tatra gāṅgeyaṃ mantrimadhye dvijarṣabha
english: "Then, seeing the marriage preparations, this maiden, the one who had been won, spoke there to the son of Gaṅgā in the midst of the counselors, O bull among the twice-born:"

sanskrit: mayā śālvapatir vīra manasābhivṛtaḥ patiḥ na mām arhasi dharmajña paracittāṃ pradāpitum
english: "'O hero, the lord of Śālva has been chosen by me in my heart as my husband; you ought not, O knower of dharma, to give me away when my heart is set on another.'"

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vacanaṃ bhīṣmaḥ saṃmantrya saha mantribhiḥ niścitya visasarjemāṃ satyavatyā mate sthitaḥ
english: "Having heard that word, Bhīṣma, after taking counsel with the ministers and reaching a decision, released her, abiding by the judgment of Satyavatī."

sanskrit: anujñātā tu bhīṣmeṇa śālvaṃ saubhapatiṃ tataḥ kanyeyaṃ muditā vipra kāle vacanam abravīt
english: "Permitted then by Bhīṣma, this maiden, glad at heart, went to Śālva, lord of Saubha, O Brāhmaṇa, and in due time spoke these words:"

sanskrit: visarjitāsmi bhīṣmeṇa dharmaṃ māṃ pratipādaya manasābhivṛtaḥ pūrvaṃ mayā tvaṃ pārthivarṣabha
english: "'I have been released by Bhīṣma; grant me my rightful place. You, O bull among kings, were earlier chosen by me in my heart.'"

sanskrit: pratyācakhyau ca śālvo 'pi cāritrasyābhiśaṅkitaḥ seyaṃ tapovanaṃ prāptā tāpasye 'bhiratā bhṛśam
english: "But Śālva refused her too, suspicious of her conduct. So she has come to the penance-grove, devoted utterly to the ascetic life."

sanskrit: mayā ca pratyabhijñātā vaṃśasya parikīrtanāt asya duḥkhasya cotpattiṃ bhīṣmam eveha manyate
english: "And I recognized her by the recital of her lineage. As for the source of this sorrow, she holds Bhīṣma alone to be its cause here."

sanskrit: ambovāca bhagavann evam evaitad yathāha pṛthivīpatiḥ śarīrakartā mātur me sṛñjayo hotravāhanaḥ
english: Ambā said: "Reverend one, it is even so, just as the king says—Hotravāhana the Sṛñjaya, the begetter of my mother's body."

sanskrit: na hy utsahe svanagaraṃ pratiyātuṃ tapodhana avamānabhayāc caiva vrīḍayā ca mahāmune
english: "For I cannot bear to return to my own city, O you whose wealth is austerity—both from fear of dishonor and from shame, O great sage."

sanskrit: yat tu māṃ bhagavān rāmo vakṣyati dvijasattama tan me kāryatamaṃ kāryam iti me bhagavan matiḥ
english: "But whatever the reverend Rāma shall bid me, O best of the twice-born, that is the deed most fit for me to do—such, reverend sir, is my resolve."

sanskrit: akṛtavraṇa uvāca duḥkhadvayam idaṃ bhadre katarasya cikīrṣasi pratikartavyam abale tat tvaṃ vatse bravīhi me
english: Akṛtavraṇa said: "This is a twofold sorrow, good lady; for which of the two do you wish redress to be wrought, O frail one? Tell me that, my child."

sanskrit: yadi saubhapatir bhadre niyoktavyo mate tava niyokṣyati mahātmā taṃ rāmas tvaddhitakāmyayā
english: "If, good lady, the lord of Saubha is to be constrained in your judgment, the great-souled Rāma will constrain him for your welfare."

sanskrit: athāpageyaṃ bhīṣmaṃ taṃ rāmeṇecchasi dhīmatā raṇe vinirjitaṃ draṣṭuṃ kuryāt tad api bhārgavaḥ
english: "But if you wish to see that Bhīṣma, son of the river, conquered in battle by the wise Rāma, the Bhārgava would do that too."

sanskrit: sṛñjayasya vacaḥ śrutvā tava caiva śucismite yad atrānantaraṃ kāryaṃ tad adyaiva vicintyatām
english: "Having heard the word of the Sṛñjaya and your own, O bright-smiling one, let what is next to be done in this matter be considered this very day."
